title: The wealth ladder: foundation, core, satellites
objectives: Place a client on the wealth ladder and say what each rung is.
Explain why each rung sits on the one below and never replaces it.
body_md:
Clients climb a wealth ladder: mutual funds form the core for everyone, PMS and AIFs are optional layers on top, added only when surplus, horizon and risk tolerance justify them. Foundation: emergency fund, insurance, costly debt cleared. Core (everyone): diversified mutual funds across equity, debt and hybrid, matched to goals. Satellite, listed (PMS): when investible surplus is well above ₹50 lakh and the client wants a concentrated, personalised portfolio and can handle bigger swings. Satellite, private (AIF): when the client can commit ₹1 crore or more, lock it up for years, and wants exposure to private equity, private credit, real estate or complex strategies. Each rung sits on top of the one below; it never replaces it.

> **Talk-track:** “Mutual funds are your foundation. PMS and AIFs can sit on top once that's solid and you can lock some money away for longer.”

> **Investor takeaway:** Build the core first. Add PMS or AIFs only with money you won't need for years.
example: ₹60 lakh investor with no MF core asking for PMS: eligible, not suitable — build the core first; PMS only as a slice later.
say: Each rung sits on the one below; it never replaces it.
never: PMS replaces the mutual fund core.
AIFs suit money needed next year.
